angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 330,458 km at 114.29 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.7499 +/- 0.0166 mas (same row, RUWE 1.06): 114.29 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.475 +/- 0.014 solar radii from Barkaoui et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2084 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..38B/abstract): 330,458 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.453 +/- 0.029 solar masses from Barkaoui et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2084 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..38B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3551 +/- 49 K from Barkaoui et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2084 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..38B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Barkaoui et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2084 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..38B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2084.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.741, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
